title: Religion Can Assuage
description: Religion Can Assuage in Tonic Solfa to SOUTHWELL, doh is Ab: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Anne Steele wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 408 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Religion a Support in Life”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Short Metre (6.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to SOUTHWELL; any other Short Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Re-li-gion can as-suage The tem-pest of the soul; And ev-ery fear shall lose its rage At her di-vine con-trol.

lines: And every fear shall lose its rage
And o'er the path her heavenly ray
Thou blest supporter of the mind,
O, let us feel thy power,

licence: Public domain: Anne Steele died in 1778.
credits: Words by Anne Steele (1717–1778), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to SOUTHWELL by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
